title: Harmonize press‑hold cancellation and theme‑adaptive ripple for compact split & icon‑only buttons
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: We've observed multiple regressions and inconsistent behaviors across compact/split and icon-only button variants after token migrations and recent motion changes. Issues: 1) high-contrast (HC) theme loses visible focus ring for icon-only and split-button primary actions; 2) press-and-hold interaction used to cancel in some flows is now committing unexpectedly on long-press on mobile/touch; 3) ripple and loading affordances cause visual reflow when toggling loading state; 4) reduced-motion users do not get consistent cancellation affordance. Goal: Define a single, accessible interaction and visual contract for compact/split/icon-only buttons across themes and motion settings, implement theme-adaptive ripple and cancel affordance, and eliminate layout shifts during loading.
acceptance_criteria: HC theme: visible focus ring for all icon-only and split-button interactive targets (contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 against surface)

Press-and-hold: long-press must show a cancel affordance (visual timer or subtle hold ring) and not trigger click until release or explicit hold-complete path; behaviour toggles correctly with reduced-motion preference
Ripple: touch/click ripple adapts color tokens per theme (light/dark/HC) and respects reduced-motion (fade-only, no scale up)
Loading state: introducing spinner or placeholder must not change button layout width/height or shift adjacent content; spinner overlays should be absolutely positioned inside canonical hit area
A11y: aria-pressed, aria-busy and accessible name flows validated with VoiceOver and TalkBack; keyboard focus and activation parity preserved
Unit/visual tests: Storybook stories for compact / icon-only / split-button covering all themes and motion prefs; Percy snapshots without visual diffs in baseline regions
design_notes: Designs live in Figma: Figma file 'Design System / Buttons — press‑hold parity' (link below). New token recommendations: introduce btn.ripple-color-{light,dark,high-contrast} and btn.cancel-ring-thickness; reuse existing spacing tokens to avoid layout changes. Proposed ripple is a 12px max radius with opacity tuned per theme. For reduced-motion, use a 140ms fade and no scale transform. For loading, convert inline spinner to absolutely positioned overlay that uses btn.icon-size token and preserves internal padding. Add a visual hold indicator (subtle radial progress) only for touch long-press flows; keyboard users see a visible focus ring and an explicit tooltip-based hint in guided flows.
implementation_notes: Engineering work: update Button component to accept new tokens and flags (rippleTheme, holdCancelable). CSS changes should be limited to variables: --btn-ripple-color, --btn-cancel-ring, --btn-spinner-offset. Avoid DOM structure changes that would break third-party selectors; prefer class toggles and CSS-only overlay when possible. Add feature flag 'btn-press-hold-cancel' for staged rollout. Add unit tests for pointer events and keyboard flow. Coordinate with ENG-19876 (token migration) and ENG-20345 (icon-button hit-target refactor).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Token migration may change color math and produce insufficient contrast — mitigation: include HC-specific token overrides and run WCAG contrast checks in CI
Risk: Third-party consumers relying on DOM structure may break — mitigation: avoid removing existing elements, instead layer overlays and keep class-based API backwards compatible
Risk: Motion changes may regress perceived responsiveness — mitigation: test reduced-motion and default motion in parallel; expose opt-out flag for a short window
qa_checklist: Verify focus ring contrast across light/dark/HC themes
Manual test long-press on iOS Safari, Android Chrome, and desktop touch emulation
Toggle reduced-motion in OS settings and confirm no scaling animations for ripple/hold
Run Storybook accessibility snapshot and Lighthouse keyboard navigation audit
Confirm no layout shifts when toggling loading in dense real-world containers
rollout_plan: Enable feature flag in staging for 48 hours, run automated visual regression and mobile touch tests, then enable for 10% of traffic in canary with monitoring on UI errors and conversion metrics for affected routes. If no regressions, ramp to 100% in next console release. Communicate changelog and migration notes to integrators.
